sections.shot: B-roll: web/public/gallery/lattice_orbit.mp4 (Blender render of the live no-three-in-line SAT snapshot), title card overlay.
sections.caption: Learning to Discover  |  an autonomous AI lab for open math problems
sections.text: This is Learning to Discover: an autonomous AI lab that hunts for records on open math problems, and improves by doing it.

sections.shot: Mission Control /: hero and totals counters, then slow scroll so the Autonomous Loop phase stepper is centred; cursor sweeps the eight phases left to right.
sections.caption: One loop every 3 min  |  35+ cycles, 850+ logged decisions, all auditable
sections.text: This is the live lab. Every 3 minutes, with no human in the loop, it reads telemetry, re-verifies every claim, recalls memory, searches papers with Exa, proposes experiments with GPT-6 Astra, has Claude Fable referee them, then executes. Over 35 cycles and 850 logged decisions so far.

sections.shot: Mission Control /: scroll to the Compute Map; hover GPU tiles, then the CPU core grid, then the Modal fleet row.
sections.caption: 8 x A100  |  124 CPU cores  |  Modal fleet 140/140 containers
sections.text: It runs on 8 A100 GPUs and 124 CPU cores, coloured by the problem that owns them, plus an elastic Modal fleet: 140 containers right now.

sections.shot: /problems/no-three-in-line-75: header (record vs ours), then the 75x75 construction canvas with red violated lines; hover two points to isolate their lines.
sections.caption: No-three-in-line 75x75  |  record 148  |  ours: 150 points, 107 violated lines (not valid yet)
sections.text: The flagship problem: no three in line, on a 75 by 75 grid. The record is 148 points. Our best candidate places 150, but 107 lines, in red, still cross three or more. Zero would be a new record. We are not there yet.

sections.shot: /decisions filtered to proposer, decision #211 expanded (rationale, queries, 3 Exa sources); cut to referee filter, #219 expanded (Claude Fable approve); cut to #191 expanded (prediction vs outcome, REFUTED).
sections.caption: Decision #211: GPT-6 Astra proposes, 3 Exa sources  |  #219: Claude Fable 5.2 approves  |  #191: prediction refuted
sections.text: Every action is a card in the audit log. Here GPT-6 Astra asks for research, citing three Exa sources. Claude Fable reviews and approves it, with its own reasoning. Launches carry a falsifiable prediction: this one expected 16 collinear triples in 30 minutes. The critic observed 17, and marked it refuted.

sections.shot: /memory: agent graph (hover the proposer node), then scroll to the Memory Benchmark bars and table.
sections.caption: past.dev shared memory: 360+ facts  |  benchmark on 31 questions: past.dev 74%, markdown 100%, RAG 97%
sections.text: Agents share memory through past.dev: over 360 facts. Benchmarked honestly, it scores 74 percent, against 100 for plain markdown and 97 for RAG.

sections.shot: /learning: Tinker RL reward curve and valid-construction curve, gen-0 vs gen-N panel, then scroll to the Modal sandboxes table.
sections.caption: Tinker RL, reward = official verifier  |  held-out valid rate 0% -> 50% in 40 steps  |  28 Modal sandbox runs
sections.text: The lab also trains itself. Tinker fine-tunes an open Qwen model with the verifier as reward: valid constructions on held-out prompts went from 0 to 50 percent in 40 steps. Devin writes new search programs, tested in Modal sandboxes; so far none has passed.

sections.shot: /gallery: Blender renders (Lattice, Hadamard City, Snake), then scroll to the three-body orbit plots (figure-eight, moth II, candidates, 7 families).
sections.caption: Three-body domain: known families rediscovered  |  candidate orbits not found in the catalogs we checked
sections.text: The same loop now runs astrophysics: periodic three-body orbits. Our GPU search rediscovered the figure-eight and other known families, and reports candidate orbits not found in the catalogs we checked.

sections.shot: B-roll: lattice_orbit.mp4 again, closing card with the replay URL.
sections.caption: No math record beaten yet  |  replay: vnmoorthy.github.io/learning-to-discover
sections.text: On the math problems, no record is beaten yet, and the app says so. Every decision, source and prediction is logged and replayable. Learning to Discover.
